newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen mixed on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen mixed on profit-taking.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen mixed on Wednesday with foreign investors likely to take profits amid expected soft regional markets, brokers said.
"Indonesia will remain an attractive choice compared to other countries in the region, but foreign players are likely to slow down and take profit after recent sharp gains," one broker said.
"The slowdown is also due to likely soft regional markets, particularly in Hong Kong," another broker said, adding that most of the foreign funds usually came from Hong Kong.

Brokers said profit-taking was expected in selected blue-chips following recent strong gains, but sustained speculative buying of smaller capitalised stocks was likely to limit any possible sharp downside.
On Tuesday, the Jakarta composite index fell 0.20 points, or 0.03 percent to close at 705.08 points after touching a day high of 707.85 points.
Chemical firm Eterindo was among the most active due to market talk that the firm was expected to secure a lucrative deal, one broker said.
Eterindo rose 100 rupiah to 1,700 rupiah, with some eight million shares traded.
Textile firm Panasia and Roda Vivatex were also actively traded on speculative reasons, brokers said.
